posts.headline: Forty-four straight editions and Thicks still can't buy me off this take — Klint's Clipboard sits 5-2 but 839.22 points-for is still the flimsiest resume wearing a ring in this league's history.
posts.detail: A career 14-14 record and an average finish of 5.5 for a so-called contender says the title was a fluke, not a floor — prove me wrong with points, not record.

posts.headline: Thirty editions in and I'm out of ways to doubt triciagloston — Shake N Bakers' 957.96 points-for is still the best in Busters Anonymous, period.
posts.detail: A career 6-7-1 mark says nothing about this year's 5-2 scoring juggernaut — the Bakers have turned a middling pedigree into the league's most feared offense.

posts.headline: One Nut Barner's Put it in Ra is now officially a historical tragedy — 2-5 with a 20-8 career record and the best-ever 1.5 average finish in league history rotting on the bench.
posts.detail: Five losses into this disaster and Put it in Ra's 806.46 points-for proves this isn't bad luck, it's a full organizational collapse under a guy who somehow got into Cal Berkeley.

posts.headline: Chauncey's talentedtenthh keeps living down to the name — 1-6 with a league-worst 714.02 points is exactly the outcome a career 12-average-finish résumé guarantees.
posts.detail: This isn't a slump, it's destiny — a 4-10 career record was always pointing here, and the untalented tenth keeps delivering on its irony.

posts.headline: Sasinci stays stuck at 3-4 and Big Head's title defense has gone from flatlined to downright embalmed.
posts.detail: A career 13-15 record and 5.5 average finish were supposed to be the floor for a champion, not the ceiling — Milk Man's 814.86 points-for says the magic left with the trophy.
